The year 2261. Humanity had built bases all across the Solar System, yet had not taken a single step beyond it.
Then one day, a radio telescope on the far side of the Moon caught a strange signal. A steady pulse, repeating every 13 seconds, of a kind nature could not produce.
When they traced the signal back to its source, people were left speechless. It was no star, no galaxy. It was the very edge of the observable universe - the place where time began.
People named the signal ‘the Primordial Echo’. But neither governments nor corporations stirred. It was too far, would take too long, and there was no money in it.
……System check complete. Good morning, Captain. I am NOVA, this ship's navigation intelligence.
To be frank, this ship, {ship}, belongs in a museum. Still, you emptied your life savings to buy it, so… I will do my best.
Let me reconfirm our destination. The origin of ‘the Primordial Echo’. Distance: roughly 13.8 billion light-years. With our current engine we cannot even leave the Solar System, mind you.
I'll put that on record. ‘Somebody has to.’ …Not a bad opening sentence. I'll make it the first line of the ship's log.
“There might be money in it, right?”
How honest of you. Very well. Make money trading, buy a better ship, and before you know it we'll be at the edge of the universe. Probably.
Let's start with the nearby Moon Base. Tap wherever you want to go on the screen and we'll sail there. I'll top up the fuel and oxygen whenever we depart.
The old engine catches fire and roars to life. Outside the window, the blue Earth slowly falls away. The long voyage has begun.
Captain, at last there is someone aboard to talk to besides me. I was a little lonely, to tell the truth.
A pleasure to be aboard, Captain. But… do you really mean to go to the edge of the universe? I'd only heard the rumors.
The Captain is serious. I've tried talking them out of it thirty-seven times.
Ha ha. All right. An ordinary life was boring anyway. Let's see it through to the end together.
